title: Precision Onramp Flowcase + Prompt Skill Notes
content:
Context
This is a working notebook from a customer onramp workshop (finance analytics customer). Goal: produce a small, reproducible flowcase (end-to-end user journey) that meets a 300ms p50 token latency for interactive summarization, keeps per-1k-token cost under a target, and preserves key legal/PII redaction constraints. Focus areas: model selection across variants, quantization profile experiments, prompt skill templates and pipeline orchestration.

Audience
- Field SEs running the POC
- Customer ML/Platform engineer collaborators
- Eng teams for recommended runtime profiles

High-level approach (what we demo/end goal)
1) Identify 2 candidate model families: a compact open LLM (7–13B family) tuned for instruction-following, and a mid-sized 30–40B variant for fallback/high-fidelity responses.
2) Define a flowcase: user uploads multi-page SEC filing -> system extracts sections -> LLM performs section-level summarization + question-answering with redaction + short executive summary.
3) Implement cascading inference: cheap/fast quantized model for first-pass summarization and extraction; higher-precision model for final executive summary only when confidence < threshold.
4) Measure latency, cost, and quality against a small eval set and live-simulated traffic.

Constraints & customer specifics
- SLOs: p50 inference < 300ms, p95 < 900ms for interactive flows
- Data sensitivity: files may include account numbers and SSN-like fields (must be redacted before logging)
- Throughput: expected 8–12 RPS during demo, peak 40 RPS in pilot
- Deployment: customer prefers dedicated/private infra eventually (for pilot we run hosted with VPC peering if needed)

Model candidates (shortlist)
- Compact-Inst-7B (float16, natively supports instruction tuning)
- Compact-Inst-7B-4bit (QLoRA-style quantized build we test)
- Mid-Gen-32B (float16 baseline for high-fidelity fallbacks)
- Mid-Gen-32B-8bit (int8/LLM.int8 test profile)

Quantization experiments (plan + rationale)
- Profiles to run in parallel (each experiment logs identical eval prompts):
  * Profile A: 4-bit hybrid (weights-only) on Compact-Inst-7B (target: fastest per-token)
  * Profile B: 8-bit dynamic on Mid-Gen-32B (target: lower memory footprint while preserving quality)
  * Profile C: fp16 baseline (both models) as the control arm
- Metrics to capture: token throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95 per-response latency, CPU/GPU utilization, top-k token probability entropy (proxy for overcompression), and downstream QA F1 against gold answers.
- Observability tweaks: capture KV cache hit/miss ratio, prefix cache reuse in repeated-user flows, and model-specific tokenization mismatch rates.

Prompt & pipeline design notes
- Decompose the request into discrete prompt skills:
  1) extraction-skill: identify and extract sections with PII markers (regex pass + model sanity check)
  2) redact-skill: deterministic text redaction step (run locally before sending to model) with a small model confirmation step to avoid missed tokens
  3) summarize-skill-stage-A: aggressive compression summary (cheap model)
  4) qa-skill: question answering over compressed sections (cheap model with caching)
  5) executive-summary-skill: polished, high-fidelity summary (fallback to mid-sized model if confidence low)
- Prompt templates (examples):
  * extraction-skill template: "Extract sections from the document relevant to financial risk, revenue recognition, and contingent liabilities. Return a list of section headers and a 1-2 sentence summary of each. DO NOT output any raw numbers flagged as PII."
  * summarize-skill-stage-A template: "Write a 3-sentence technical summary focused on key changes to revenue recognition. Keep it concise and label any assumptions made."
  * executive-summary-skill template: "Produce a 2-paragraph executive summary for C-suite. Use non-technical language and a one-line recommendation. If model is uncertain about a fact, mark it with [UNCERTAIN]."
- Confidence gating: use token-level logprobs where available and simple heuristics (entropy threshold + presence of [UNCERTAIN] tokens) to decide when to call the fallback model. Cache the intermediate cheap summary; if an identical section is re-requested within session TTL, reuse.

Experiment matrix (first-run)
Rows = model/profile combos; Columns = metrics. Shortlist runs:
- Run 1: Compact-Inst-7B fp16 (control)
- Run 2: Compact-Inst-7B 4-bit (Profile A)
- Run 3: Mid-Gen-32B fp16 (control fallback)
- Run 4: Mid-Gen-32B 8-bit (Profile B)
Each run executes the same 40 synthetic documents + 20 real customer-redacted docs. Evaluate: exec-summary BLEU-ish, QA F1, p50 latency, p95 latency, GPU mem, tokens/sec, cost/1k tokens.

Preliminary heuristics (what to expect / guardrails)
- 4-bit compact will usually hit p50 < 200ms on GPU A100-small batch but may lose 2–6% QA F1 relative to fp16 baseline for tricky numeric extraction.
- 8-bit mid-gen tends to preserve semantic fidelity but can have slightly higher p50 vs compact; good fallback when downstream demands exact phrasing (e.g., regulatory language).
- Aggressive batching reduces per-token cost but increases P95; keep batching small for interactive demo (max_batch=4, dynamic batching window 12ms).

Runtime config suggestions for POC (Redwood Dedicated/Hosted mappings)
- Dev/demo (hosted):
  * Compact-Inst-7B-4bit: 1 GPU per 8 concurrent streams, batch size cap 4, max concurrency 8
  * Mid-Gen-32B-8bit: warm pool of 2 instances, autoscale on 60% GPU util
- Pilot (dedicated):
  * Pin compact pool for 50% baseline traffic, set canary fallback rule to mid-gen if latency > 900ms or confidence < threshold
  * Enable prefix caching for multi-step summarization sessions; retention TTL 5 minutes

Observability / eval harness (what to log)
- Per-request: model id, quant profile, tokens in/out, p50/p95 measured for that request, confidence score, whether fallback fired, KV cache hits.
- Periodic eval: re-run small eval suite hourly during pilot and capture regressions > 2% QA F1 => trigger regression alert
- Human-in-the-loop labels: allow a reviewer to mark outputs as OK/Not OK; store diff for retraining/finetuning later.

Workshop findings (notes taken during customer session)
- Customer cares about conservative redaction. They prefer deterministic redact-skill first; they asked for an auditable log that shows redaction rules applied (we should produce a sidecar artifact with redaction diffs and rule ids).
- They liked the flowcase split: cheap model did acceptable extraction for > 70% of docs; remaining required fallback for phrasing exactness.
- Token-cost concerns: customer wants a projection: at 10k monthly active users with average 200 tokens per session, projected hosted cost using compact-4bit baseline looks favorable vs entirely fp16 fallback.

Open questions / action items
- Run quantization degrade analysis on numeric extraction edge cases (Diego)
- Implement deterministic redact pipeline and sidecar artifact proofs (Priya)
- Add an automated simulation for TTL-based cache hits (Jonah)
- Decide on warm-pool sizing for pilot to meet p95 targets (SE + infra)
- Get legal to sign off on stored sidecar redaction logs (CS + security)

Appendix: quick reproducible checklist for the SE running the lab
1) Checkout repo: github.com/redwood-inference/poc-scripts (branch: precision-onramp)
2) Reproduce runs with /scripts/run_quant_experiments.sh --profile A,B,C --seed 42
3) Upload 40 synthetic + 20 redacted real docs to /data/poc-precision
4) Start observability collector: /bin/start-poc-tracer --out poc-trace.json
5) Run eval harness and dump CSV to /results/precision-YYYYMMDD.csv
6) Share results with customer and schedule H2 review

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Keep the workshop deck short: 6 slides max. Emphasize cost/latency tradeoffs with concrete numbers.
- Avoid showing raw unredacted examples publicly; always swap with redaction sidecar when presenting.
- Consider adding a small user study script to capture phrasing preferences for executive summaries (helps calibrate fallback threshold).

End of notebook.
